paragraphs: The EU’s anti-deforestation law faces an enforcement test ahead of its launch on 30 December 2026.
Under the new rules, companies selling goods such as palm oil, coffee, and cocoa must prove their products are not linked to land cleared after 2020.

However, recent investigations by Indonesian environmental organizations reveal that major international consumer brands risk breaching these regulations. Reports show that companies like PepsiCo, Unilever, and Ferrero have bought palm oil from Indonesian plantations accused of recent illegal deforestation. Despite heavy political pressure and lobbying from major exporting nations like the United States and Indonesia to delay or soften the legislation, environmental activists insist the EU must strictly enforce the rules.

Indonesia has lost vast areas of forest to illegal logging and agricultural clearing, which increased its vulnerability to severe wildfires. Experts emphasize that strict enforcement by European authorities will be essential to hold global corporations accountable and halt worldwide forest destruction.

paragraphs: The EU will start using new anti-deforestation rules on 30 December 2026. Companies which sell products like palm oil, coffee, and chocolate must prove they don’t cut down trees to make them.

But environmental groups in Indonesia found that big international brands may be breaking these rules. Well-known companies like PepsiCo and Unilever recently bought palm oil from plantations linked to illegal forest clearing.

Some countries, including the US and Indonesia, asked the EU to make the rules easier for businesses. But environmental activists say Europe must stay strong and enforce the law. Indonesia lost many forests to farming and fires, so strict checks are needed to protect nature and stop global forest destruction.

paragraphs: The EU has a new rule to save forests. The rule is starting on 30 December 2026. Companies which sell things like coffee, palm oil, and chocolate must prove that they do not cut down trees.
But some big companies are still buying palm oil from places in Indonesia. People cut down forests illegally there.

Some countries want Europe to stop or change the rule. These countries are, for example, the US and Indonesia. But the EU must follow the rules strictly. Indonesia is losing many trees to big fires and farming. People hope that this new rule will stop companies from harming trees and help keep the earth green and safe.
